newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-CARPENTIER STAKES CLAIM TO CHALLENGE TRACY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-CARPENTIER STAKES CLAIM TO CHALLENGE TRACY.

text.p: Patrick Carpentier staked a claim as a threat to end fellow Canadian Paul Tracy's three-race winning streak in the CART IndyCar series in unofficial practice Friday for Sunday's Milwaukee 200.
Carpentier, driving in only his seventh race in the series, blistered the venerable one-mile Milwaukee oval with a lap of 20.397 seconds or 182.144 mph (293.124 kph) in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz.

Mauricio Gugelmin of Brazil was only eight thousandths of a second off the pace at 20.405 seconds, also in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz. Tracy, the series points leader, wasn't far off the pace with a lap of 20.572 in a Penske Mercedes-Benz.
Last Sunday the two Canadians put on a dramatic show in the closing stages of the St Louis 300 with Tracy taking the lead because Carpentier had to slow to conserve methanol fuel.
Carpentier's Bettenhausen Motorsports can smell the first victory for the team and their 25-year-old driver.

"It sure helps," Carpentier said. "In the last three races we've been close, the confidence is growing, but I know we'll have a struggle ... I never thought it would happen in the first half of the season.
"We really have good engineers, and it shows."
Tracy, now the wily veteran at 28 with 13 wins in his column, doesn't disagree. "He doesn't have a lot of experience, but when you have engineers like he does it helps."
Scott Pruett of the Unites States, winner of the Surfers Paradise race, was fourth in a Reynard Ford at 20.634 seconds. Canadian Greg Moore was fifth at 20.646 seconds in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
The 27-car field was tightly bunched, all slower than the track record of 21.719 seconds set by Raul Boesel of Brazil in 1993, in part due to a track repaving programme.
Official qualifying for Sunday's 200-mile (322 km) race was to be held on Saturday.
